scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund policy window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Meredith Hughes and I'm 76. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Meredith, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it is to return from a trip and find an unexpected charge, especially when you believed you had already canceled the service. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Of course. My account number is 8829-4410 and the email is m.hughes@email.com.

Thank you, Meredith. I have successfully verified your account. I can see the cancellation request was logged on the system 34 days ago, but the billing cycle processed the renewal charge shortly thereafter. While our 'Service Terms and Conditions' section 4.2 strictly stipulates a 30-day window for refund requests, I can see this is a genuine oversight due to your travel.
I really appreciate you looking into that. It was just a complete oversight on my part.

You are very welcome. Given your long-standing history with us, I have received approval to grant a one-time exception to our policy. I have processed a full refund of $49.99 to your original payment method. You should see the credit appear on your statement within 3 to 5 business days.
Oh, that is such a relief. Thank you so much for your help today, I really appreciate it.
It was my pleasure, Meredith. I have sent a confirmation of this refund to your email address. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account, acknowledged the policy constraint, and utilized a one-time exception authority to process a full refund for the customer.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified the account efficiently using the requested credentials and demonstrated high empathy by acknowledging the customer's specific situation. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited section 4.2 of the policy while utilizing their authority to grant a valid, one-time exception without requiring an unnecessary escalation.
